newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firmer with Dated headed upwards.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firmer with Dated headed upwards.

text.p: The North Sea crude market was firm on Friday with Dated Brent seen recovering from trading plays which pushed values well below October Brent parity, traders said.
Bids for wet Brent cargoes were heard at Oct Brent +5 cents in late talk, after a 13-15 cargo had traded earlier at Oct -7 cents.
The same cargo had been bought by a trading arm of a major oil company on Thursday at Oct parity, was sold to an affiliate at Oct -5 cents and then resold at Oct -10 cents.
"(The major) is trying to push the market down..possibly it's a short swaps position," said one trader.
Traders said that the strength of cfds confirmed that the market was firmer than the Brent trades implied.
Cfds for next week traded at Oct evens, while Sep 16-20 traded at Oct Brent -6 cents.
Bids on wet Brent were heard at Oct Brent +5 cents in late talk.
Oct Brent was talked around IPE screen levels which was trading up 24 cents at $22.40 a barrel by 1751 GMT.
Traders said the North sea market's relative buoyancy, despite a well-supplied prompt Brent market, was partly due to the strength of gas oil futures and physical markets.
"A lot of it has to do with the gas oil squeeze," said one North Sea producer. "The gas oil-rich grades are benefitting."
The trader said that gas oil demand was behind the flurry of deals on North sea grades on Thursday, particularly Forties.
A Statfjord cargo, loading 24-26, traded at a strong Dated Brent +30, against a deal on Wednesday at Dated Brent +14 cents.
Of six Brent dates turning wet today, four were kept, one was deferred and one was clocked, traders said.
